paragraphs: Here's what I want you to carry out of this one, friend. Joshua tells his commanders, "Do not be afraid or discouraged… Be strong and courageous, for the LORD will do this to all the enemies you fight." (Joshua 10:25) Notice the reason he gives. It isn't that Israel is tough. It's what the LORD will do. That's where courage comes from, and it's a LOT sturdier than the kind you build up in the mirror.

The writer wraps up the whole campaign with one line: "because the LORD, the God of Israel, fought for Israel, Joshua captured all these kings and their land in one campaign." (Joshua 10:42) Five kings, a pile of fortified cities, and the text gives the credit to the LORD. This is also a heavy passage, and the text says plainly that it happened as the LORD, the God of Israel, had commanded (Joshua 10:40). I think the lesson is to trust Him to be the One who fights, and not to dress up our own strength as the hero.

So what does that mean for you on a Monday morning? You'll face some hard stuff: a bill, a boss, a day that already feels too big. Be strong and courageous, but let your courage rest on the same thing Joshua's did. I tried standing on my own strength once, and I'm a cookie stamper, so it was a short conversation. The LORD fights for His people, and that's something you can stand on.
